statement: The installed Devin binary has no command surface: devin --help lists no commands subcommand, and devin skills is documented as 'Manage agent skills (slash commands and agent-triggered context blobs)' — Devin's slash commands ARE skills.
Devin's only non-skill prompt-injection surfaces are --prompt-file <FILE> and the [PROMPT]... argument after --; neither registers a discoverable command entry point.
Devin's retired command mirror lived at .devin/skills/<cmd>/SKILL.md (35 entries at removal), not .devin/commands; a Devin command mirror is loadable only in skill shape.
evidence: git show a2241041b0 body: 'removes all 35 .devin/skills/<cmd>/SKILL.md mirrors'

statement: Removal of the Devin command surface was an explicit operator directive with a BREAKING CHANGE note, reversing an earlier goal-hook packet; it is a decision, not drift.
evidence: git show a2241041b0: 'per operator directive... BREAKING CHANGE: the Devin CLI no longer exposes any mirrored slash-command'

statement: The July decommission was partially reversed for the goal surface: .opencode/hooks/goal/devin/ and .devin/hooks/goal-inject.mjs exist again and are registered on SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit, while .devin/skills remains absent.
evidence: shell ls .opencode/hooks/goal/ -> devin dir with goal-inject.mjs + test

statement: Devin's replacement affordance is native discovery of the 12 .opencode/skills/* packets as slash commands; none of the 35 authored .opencode/commands entry points (speckit, deep, create, doctor) has any Devin representation, so the /speckit:* lifecycle is unavailable in Devin.

Two Devin artifacts still describe the removed command surface: SYNC.md:74 uses '36 commands' as a present-tense teaching example, and the decommission commit explicitly deferred playbook scenarios DV-014..DV-016 for rewrite.

The 35 removed .devin/skills/<cmd>/ entries are stated as a count, not a roster; whether it maps one-to-one onto today's 35 authored commands is unconfirmed. Confirming check: list deleted paths in a2241041b0 and diff against the current command tree.
